bull_case: Planet can reinvest in higher-resolution, hyperspectral and software capabilities while revenue scales faster than fleet cost. Positive H1 FCF and large backlog suggest the business can cross into self-funded compounding if capex intensity falls.
bear_case: The model remains capital intensive: fleet replacement, launches, R&D and SBC can absorb much of enterprise growth. Recent positive cash flow benefited from deferred revenue and receivable movements, while ATM and warrant issuance diluted owners.
thesis: Reinvestment runway is large but incremental ROIC and FCF/share quality are not yet proven. FY27 H1 OCF was $68.4M and reported FCF $21.3M, yet OCF benefited from a $47.1M increase in deferred revenue and a $23.9M receivables decline. H1 PP&E purchases were $44.7M, SBC $33.5M, and the company raised $122.4M gross via ATM plus $107.8M from warrant exercises. This is adequate for a Moonshot but far below a mature Compounder profile.

evidence.claim: FY27 H1 operating cash flow was $68.4M; reported FCF was $21.3M and PP&E purchases were $44.7M.
H1 OCF benefited from a $47.1M increase in deferred revenue and $23.9M decrease in accounts receivable, so current cash generation includes working-capital timing.
H1 stock-based compensation was $33.5M; unrecognized RSU compensation was $149.5M over about 2.2 years.
The company sold 3.78M shares through its ATM for $122.4M gross in Q2 and received $107.8M from public-warrant exercises in H1.
FY27 revenue guidance of $430M-$441M and capex guidance of $100M-$115M imply capex remains roughly one quarter of revenue at the current scale.

counterevidence: Revenue growth and backlog are strong enough that fixed fleet and platform investments can gain operating leverage.
Positive H1 FCF marks a real improvement from prior negative cash generation.
ATM shares were sold at $31.95 average net price, materially above the frozen $16.99 price, making that specific issuance less value-destructive than low-price financing.
A large cash and investment balance gives management time to prove capital efficiency.
unknowns: Maintenance versus growth share of fleet capex.
Normalized FCF after working-capital timing effects.
Long-run SBC and net dilution rate.
Incremental gross profit per dollar of Pelican/Tanager investment.

uncertainties.rationale: Strong demand is evident, but full-cycle fleet and software returns are not yet measurable.
Multiple products, geographies and government/commercial use cases provide a long runway.
Working-capital timing, SBC, ATM and warrant issuance materially complicate current per-share FCF.

falsifiers: Capex and SBC remain proportional to revenue such that normalized FCF/share fails to compound.
Incremental satellite deployments do not produce gross-profit growth above their full lifecycle cost.
Net share dilution remains persistently high after the company has achieved sustainable positive FCF.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Incremental ROIC is unproven, but strong revenue/RPO growth and emerging positive FCF do not show a structural collapse.

Recent ATM, warrant issuance and significant SBC make dilution material. It is not yet a proven long-term veto, but must decline as FCF matures; persistent mid-to-high single-digit annual net dilution would trigger the veto.

key_kpis.name: Normalized FCF/share
key_kpis.threshold: Positive after normalizing working capital and compounding faster than diluted shares

key_kpis.name: Net dilution
key_kpis.threshold: Share-count growth trends toward low single digits or less

subscores.rationale: Demand and operating leverage are promising, but full-cycle satellite returns remain uncertain.
Persistent monitoring, sovereign services, higher-resolution/hyperspectral data and AI provide multiple long-duration reinvestment paths.
Positive FCF is emerging, but working capital, SBC and recent equity issuance materially weaken current per-share quality.
